newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says Bhutto's removal will not affect ties.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Bhutto's removal will not affect ties.

text.p: An Iranian cabinet minister said on Tuesday the dismissal of Pakistan's Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was an internal affair that would not affect the two neighbouring countries' ties.
"A change of government in Pakistan will have no effect on the strategic ties between Tehran and Islamabad," said Deputy Foreign Minister Abbas Maleki, quoted by the daily Kayhan.
"This is an internal problem, and the appearance and fall of governments is natural in party and parliamentary systems," Maleki added.
Pakistani President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto's government on Tuesday, accusing it of corruption and misrule.
"Of course we and Pakistan have had differences over Afghanistan but this has never hurt our good bilateral ties," Maleki said.
Iran and Pakistan have had close ties but differences between them surfaced after the emergence of the Taleban Islamic movement in neighbouring Afghanistan.
Iranian media have accused Pakistan of setting up the Taleban with backing from the United States and funding from Saudi Arabia to counter Iran's influence in the region.
Pakistan denies the charge and says it has no favourites among Afghan factions.
State-run Tehran radio welcomed the "Pakistani army's neutral stand in the political developments of that country."
"The caretaker government of Meraj Khalid...has a long way to go in balancing Pakistan's foreign policy," the radio added in a political commentary.
Caretaker prime minister Khalid took his oath of office on Tuesday.
The hardline daily Kayhan blasted Bhutto as an ally of the United States in Afghanistan and on the domestic scene.
"She was unaware of the fact that...America's regional allies have a (short) expiry date and are discarded after use," the newspaper said.
